uncited: Viewing direction $d \in \mathbb{R}^3$ (normalized).
LiDAR point cloud data (used to compute $\phi_L(x)$).
Hash grid structure (used to compute $\phi_h(x)$).
Per-sample density $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$.
Density embedding $h \in \mathbb{R}^k$ (dimension $k$ depends on MLP architecture).
View-dependent color $c \in \mathbb{R}^3$.
*   **Hash Grid:** A set of $L$ levels, where level $l$ has resolution $T_l$ and $F$ feature dimensions per entry.
*   **LiDAR Feature $\phi_L(x)$:** Computed from $K$ nearest LiDAR points $p_i$ to $x$.
Here $f_{i,x}$ represents the feature vector associated with point $p_i$ at location $x$ (typically identity or position offset).
**Compute LiDAR Encoding:** Identify the $K$ nearest neighbors of $x$ in the LiDAR point cloud.
Calculate weights $w_i$ and aggregate features to produce $\phi_L(x)$.
**Compute Hash Encoding:** Query the hash grid at location $x$ to produce the feature vector $\phi_h(x)$.
**Predict Color:** Concatenate the density embedding $h$ with the directional encoding $SH(d)$ to form $v_{color} = [h, SH(d)]$.
*   **Time Complexity:** Dominated by the nearest neighbor search for LiDAR points ($O(N \log N)$ or $O(N)$ with spatial indexing) and the hash grid queries ($O(1)$ average).
The MLP inference is linear in the number of samples.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Depends on the size of the hash grid and the storage of LiDAR points.
*   **Strengths:** Robustness in low-texture regions due to LiDAR geometric priors; efficient representation via hash encoding.
*   **When to use:** Street scene reconstruction where LiDAR data is available.
*   **When not to use:** Scenes without LiDAR data or where real-time performance is constrained by nearest neighbor search overhead.
By fusing LiDAR-derived features with hash-encoded features, it aims to improve reconstruction quality and robustness.
